Name: Manager Event Message Registry
Description: This registry defines messages to be used by a service to indicate conditions or configuration changes related to a manager.  The affected manager may provide the Redfish service.

ManagerReset.Description: Indicates that a manager reset occurred.
ManagerReset.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that a manager reset occurred.
ManagerReset.Message: Manager '%1' performed a '%2' type of reset.
ManagerReset.Example: Manager 'Manager1' performed a 'ForceRestart' type of reset.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager that was reset.
The type of reset that occurred.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies the affected manager.
This argument shall contain the type of reset that occurred.  This argument shall contain one of the values of the `ResetType` enumeration from the `Resource` schema.

ManagerResetWatchdogTimer.Description: Indicates that a manager reset occurred due to a watchdog timer action.
ManagerResetWatchdogTimer.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that a manager reset occurred due to a watchdog timer action.
ManagerResetWatchdogTimer.Message: Manager '%1' performed a '%2' type of reset due to watchdog timer action.
ManagerResetWatchdogTimer.Example: Manager 'Manager1' performed a 'ForceRestart' type of reset due to watchdog timer action.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager that was reset.
The type of reset that occurred.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies the affected manager.
This argument shall contain the type of reset that occurred.  This argument shall contain one of the values of the `ResetType` enumeration from the `Resource` schema.
ManagerResetWatchdogTimer.Resolution: Check additional diagnostic data if available.

ManagerSwitchedToBackupSoftwareImage.Description: Indicates that a manager switched to a backup software image.
ManagerSwitchedToBackupSoftwareImage.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that a manager is using a backup software image.
ManagerSwitchedToBackupSoftwareImage.Message: Manager '%1' switched to a backup software image.
ManagerSwitchedToBackupSoftwareImage.Example: Manager 'Manager1' switched to a backup software image.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies the affected manager.
ManagerSwitchedToBackupSoftwareImage.Resolution: Check additional diagnostic data if available.

ManagerGoingOfflineTemporarily.Description: Indicates that a manager is going offline temporarily, such as due to a maintenance operation.
ManagerGoingOfflineTemporarily.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that a manager is going offline temporarily.
ManagerGoingOfflineTemporarily.Message: Manager '%1' is going offline temporarily and should be available again in %2 seconds; clients should allow for up to %3 seconds before taking action.
ManagerGoingOfflineTemporarily.Example: Manager 'BMC' is going offline temporarily and should be available again in 120 seconds; clients should allow for up to 600 seconds before taking action.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager.
The duration the manager is expected to be offline in seconds.
The duration clients should allow for the manager to be offline in seconds.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies the affected manager.
This argument shall contain the duration the manager is expected to be offline in seconds.
This argument shall contain the duration clients should allow for the manager to be offline in seconds.
ManagerGoingOfflineTemporarily.Resolution: Wait the specified amount of time before accessing the service again.

RedundancyGroupCritical.Description: Indicates that a manager redundancy group has a critical status.
RedundancyGroupCritical.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that a manager redundancy group is operating in a critical state due to a fault or a change in configuration.
RedundancyGroupCritical.Message: Manager redundancy group '%1' is in a critical state.
RedundancyGroupCritical.Example: Manager redundancy group 'BmcRedundancy' is in a critical state.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager redundancy group.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies or describes the group of `Manager` resources.

RedundancyGroupWarning.Description: Indicates that a manager redundancy group has a warning status.
RedundancyGroupWarning.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that a manager redundancy group is operating with a warning status or in a non-redundant state due to a fault or a change in configuration.
RedundancyGroupWarning.Message: Manager redundancy group '%1' is in a warning state.
RedundancyGroupWarning.Example: Manager redundancy group 'BmcRedundancy' is in a warning state.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager redundancy group.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies or describes the group of `Manager` resources.

RedundancyGroupNormal.Description: Indicates that a manager redundancy group has returned to normal operations.
RedundancyGroupNormal.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that a manager redundancy group has returned to a normal operating state.
RedundancyGroupNormal.Message: Manager redundancy group '%1' is operating normally.
RedundancyGroupNormal.Example: Manager redundancy group 'BmcRedundancy' is operating normally.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager redundancy group.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies or describes the group of `Manager` resources.

RedundancyDisabled.Description: Indicates that a manager redundancy group was manually disabled.
RedundancyDisabled.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that a manager redundancy group was manually disabled by a client.
RedundancyDisabled.Message: Redundancy on redundancy group '%1' was manually disabled.
RedundancyDisabled.Example: Redundancy on redundancy group 'BmcRedundancy' was manually disabled.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the redundancy group.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies the affected redundancy group.
RedundancyDisabled.Resolution: Re-enable redundancy if it was disabled unintentionally.

PeerMissing.Description: Indicates that the peer manager cannot be detected.
PeerMissing.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that the peer manager cannot be detected and redundancy is therefore unavailable.
PeerMissing.Message: The peer manager of '%1' is missing.
PeerMissing.Example: The peer manager of 'Manager1' is missing.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager reporting the condition.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies the manager that detected the missing peer.
PeerMissing.Resolution: Check that the peer manager is installed, powered, and connected.

PeerUnavailable.Description: Indicates that the peer manager is present but not responding.
PeerUnavailable.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that the peer manager is present but not responding, and redundancy is therefore unavailable.
PeerUnavailable.Message: The peer manager of '%1' is not responding.
PeerUnavailable.Example: The peer manager of 'Manager1' is not responding.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager reporting the condition.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies the manager that detected the unresponsive peer.
PeerUnavailable.Resolution: Check the peer manager for errors and verify its health status.

PeerNotProvisioned.Description: Indicates that the peer manager is not provisioned.
PeerNotProvisioned.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that the peer manager is present but is not provisioned, and redundancy is therefore unavailable.
PeerNotProvisioned.Message: The peer manager of '%1' is not provisioned.
PeerNotProvisioned.Example: The peer manager of 'Manager1' is not provisioned.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager reporting the condition.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies the manager that detected the unprovisioned peer.
PeerNotProvisioned.Resolution: Complete provisioning of the peer manager.

PeerInvalidState.Description: Indicates that the peer manager is not in a valid state for redundancy.
PeerInvalidState.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that the peer manager is not in a valid state to establish redundancy, and redundancy is therefore unavailable.
PeerInvalidState.Message: The peer manager of '%1' is not in a valid state for redundancy.
PeerInvalidState.Example: The peer manager of 'Manager1' is not in a valid state for redundancy.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager reporting the condition.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies the manager that detected the invalid state on the peer.
PeerInvalidState.Resolution: Check the peer manager state and ensure it is configured correctly for redundancy.

PeerVersionMismatch.Description: Indicates that the managers in the redundancy group are running mismatched firmware versions, preventing redundancy.
PeerVersionMismatch.LongDescription: This message shall indicate that the managers in the redundancy group are running mismatched firmware versions, and redundancy is therefore unavailable.
PeerVersionMismatch.Message: Manager '%1' and its peer are running mismatched firmware versions.
PeerVersionMismatch.Example: Manager 'Manager1' and its peer are running mismatched firmware versions.
ArgDescriptions: The name or identifier of the manager reporting the condition.
ArgLongDescriptions: This argument shall contain a string that identifies the manager that detected the firmware version mismatch.
PeerVersionMismatch.Resolution: Update both managers to the same firmware version.
